Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman traces crisis contagion through retained mortgage exposures and CDS, criticizes underwriting due diligence, and argues that post-crisis capital and liquidity rules made large banks safer. He explains SVB as concentrated uninsured funding combined with duration risk, then favors targeted regulatory easing and consolidation. Primary records support the core SVB mechanism and substantial post-crisis recapitalization. Important qualifications concern HTM accounting, blanket bailout protection, nonrandom due-diligence samples and claims that SVB posed no systemic danger. The concluding multi-year bank outlook remains conditional and only partly observable.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

<a id="7aW_z6Y8cKs-c004"></a>
### 004. A CDS can hedge an owned bond or express a negative credit view without owning the bond.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 4:59-7:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7aW_z6Y8cKs&t=299s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Under the stated contract, protection payments offset reference-credit losses for a bondholder, while an unhedged protection buyer gains exposure to deterioration without owning the bond. Actual settlement includes recovery value or delivery obligations and premium costs.

Conditional reasoning: Under the stated contract, protection payments offset reference-credit losses for a bondholder, while an unhedged protection buyer gains exposure to deterioration without owning the bond. Actual settlement includes recovery value or delivery obligations and premium costs.

Assessment test: Inspect reference obligations, premium, credit events, settlement and collateral terms.


<a id="7aW_z6Y8cKs-c005"></a>
### 005. A CDS hedge remains dependent on the protection seller’s ability to pay, so interconnected dealer exposures can transmit distress.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 7:13-8:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7aW_z6Y8cKs&t=433s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Primary records identify interconnected exposures and the AIG CDS intervention. The hedge mechanism does not eliminate counterparty or collateral-liquidity risk.

Assessment test: Measure net exposure after collateral, enforceable netting and wrong-way risk, not merely gross notional.

- [Financial Statistics for the United States and the Crisis](https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2010/201020/index.html) (2010-04-15): Research identifies leverage, short-term funding and shared exposures as core vulnerabilities. Loan-vintage data show worsening early-payment defaults, reaching about 8% for 2007 loans within one year, and explain why aggregate data can conceal risk.
- [Maiden Lane transactions, terms and overview](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/maidenlane) (historical transaction record, inspected 2026-11-10): Bear transaction purchased about $30 billion of designated assets, financed by a $28.82 billion senior Fed loan and $1.15 billion subordinated JPMorgan loan absorbing first losses. This was not an indemnity against all Bear losses. AIG facilities addressed both securities lending and CDS pressure.

<a id="7aW_z6Y8cKs-c012"></a>
### 012. The 2009 stress tests and required recapitalizations restored confidence that banks could survive and helped end the crisis.

- [Supervisory Capital Assessment Program update](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/bcreg20091109a.htm) (2009-11-09): Ten institutions required $74.6 billion extra capital; nine met or exceeded buffers by November and the tenth was working with Treasury. Capital actions raised Tier 1 common equity by over $77 billion. Announcement describes improved confidence, without isolating its causal share.

Capital requirements stay in place until 2027. Model results are not guarantees against every shock.

### 020. Less stringent liquidity requirements and long transitions for midsize banks enabled SVB to take risks that larger institutions faced stronger constraints against.

<a id="7aW_z6Y8cKs-c022"></a>
### 022. Funding fixed-rate long bonds with repricing deposits exposes a bank to falling bond values and potentially negative interest spreads when rates rise.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 25:00-26:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7aW_z6Y8cKs&t=1500s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Holding fixed promised cash flows and credit risk constant, a higher discount rate lowers bond value. If funding reprices above asset yield, the financed position earns a negative interest spread. Hedge and deposit behavior can modify the result.

Conditional reasoning: Holding fixed promised cash flows and credit risk constant, a higher discount rate lowers bond value. If funding reprices above asset yield, the financed position earns a negative interest spread. Hedge and deposit behavior can modify the result.

Assessment test: Model asset duration, deposit beta, hedges and funding maturities under rate shocks.


<a id="7aW_z6Y8cKs-c023"></a>
### 023. Unrealized securities losses are deducted from book equity but do not enter earnings until securities are sold.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 25:55-26:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7aW_z6Y8cKs&t=1555s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This broadly describes available-for-sale treatment, but the Fed explains that held-to-maturity securities remain at amortized historical cost. SVB’s large HTM portfolio makes the omitted distinction material.

Assessment test: Separate AFS, HTM, trading and regulatory AOCI treatment before comparing book and economic equity.

- [Evolution of Silicon Valley Bank, supervisory review](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2023-April-SVB-Evolution-of-Silicon-Valley-Bank.htm) (2023-04-28): At 2022 year end 94% of deposits were uninsured, securities 55% of assets and HTM 78% of securities. HTM was mostly long agency MBS and carried at amortized cost. VC funding slowed and cash burn drained deposits. March 8 AFS sale lost $1.8 billion; March 9 outflows exceeded $40 billion; bank closed March 10.

### 028. Long-dated expected cash flows make high-growth, cash-burning companies particularly sensitive to higher discount rates.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

For fixed positive future cash flows, present value falls when the discount rate rises, and later cash flows have greater rate sensitivity. Financing constraints and changing forecasts add risks beyond this arithmetic.

Conditional reasoning: For fixed positive future cash flows, present value falls when the discount rate rises, and later cash flows have greater rate sensitivity. Financing constraints and changing forecasts add risks beyond this arithmetic.

Assessment test: Hold cash-flow forecasts fixed to isolate duration, then test financing and earnings changes separately.

## Framework and tools

- Examine where distributed credit risk ultimately remains.
- A hedge adds counterparty dependence rather than eliminating all risk.
- Distinguish asset credit risk, duration risk and liability concentration.
- Assess regulation through behavior and unintended consequences, not only stated intentions.
- Separate earnings pressure from immediate liquidity failure, while recognizing economic capital losses.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Illustrative GE bond plus CDS premium
- Clayton loan-file samples and defect rates
- 2009 bank stress tests and capital raises
- SVB asset duration, uninsured deposits, unrealized losses and VC cash burn
- Bank deposit-share and compliance/technology scale comparisons
- June 27, 2025 stress-test results

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
- Opening montage repeats the substantive discussion.
- December upload contains references framed around June 27, 2025; recording date is not established, so policy announcements before publication are not automatically credited as forecasts.
- Names including Tarullo, Paulson and Geithner are garbled in captions but identifiable.
- He explicitly labels the theory that Geithner stopped prosecutions as unproven; it is not extracted as his factual assertion.
